title: Google Review NFC Cards For Checkout Counters
summary: This page is for businesses that want to ask for Google reviews right at checkout and need a prompt format that works in a short, high-speed payment moment without creating friction.
heroPoints: Checkout review prompts must fit a fast, transactional moment with minimal extra explanation.
Cards, stickers and stands each change how visible and actionable the review prompt becomes at the counter.
The first pilot should test actual completion, not just whether the prompt looks noticeable enough to staff.
imageAlt: Google review card planning for checkout counters

brief.label: Best for
items: Retail counters, restaurant tills, salon checkouts and service desks asking for more local reviews.
Teams that want a branded review prompt instead of a paper QR sign near payment terminals.
Operators comparing a quick tap card handoff with a fixed prompt visible during payment.

brief.label: What to confirm
items: How long customers stop at checkout and whether staff can introduce the review prompt naturally.
Whether the best format is a hand-delivered card, a sticker on the till area or a small stand on the counter.
Phone mix, QR fallback and how often customers have free hands during payment or bagging.
Pilot quantity, number of counters and whether different store or counter types need separate tests.

faq.question: What usually works best at checkout: a card or a sticker?
faq.answer: It depends on whether staff can reliably hand over a card and whether the customer has enough time and free attention to tap or scan during payment.

faq.question: What should be tested first at a checkout counter?
faq.answer: The best first test measures customer response, payment-speed impact, staff prompting comfort and whether the phone interaction actually fits the counter workflow.
